summation.displayName: A unique, error-prone mismatch repair pathway (also called n...
summation.text:
A unique, error-prone mismatch repair pathway (also called non-canonical mismatch repair) operates in germinal center B cells (reviewed in Zanotti and Gearhart 2016, Pilzecker and Jacobs 2019) to produce about 65% of the mutations that occur at A:T base pairs in variable regions of immunoglobulin genes during somatic hypermutation (IJspeert et al. 2019, inferred from mice in Frieder et al. 2009).
MSH2:MSH6, also called MutSalpha, binds G:U mismatches in vitro (Wilson et al. 2005) and, based on phenotypes of individuals lacking MSH2 or MSH6, MSH2:MSH6 is concluded to bind G:U mismatches produced by AICDA during somatic hypermutation (IJspeert et al. 2019). MSH2:MSH3, also called MutSbeta does not appear to affect somatic hypermutation (inferred from mice in Martomo et al. 2004). After binding a mismatch, the MSH2:MSH6 heterodimer exchanges ADP for ATP, which alters its conformation to a sliding clamp or molecular switch able to diffuse in one direction along duplex DNA (Gradia et al. 1997, Blackwell et al. 1998, Gradia et al. 1999, Gradia et al. 2000). MSH2:MSH6 then recruits MLH1:PMS2 (MutLalpha) to form a ternary complex with mismatched DNA (Gu et al. 1998, Blackwell et al. 2001, Plotz et al. 2002).
The latent endonuclease activity of MLH1:PMS2 (MutLalpha) is activated by interaction with MSH2:MSH6 (Kadyrov et al 2006) and MLH1:PMS2 makes a single strand nick in DNA. Individuals that lack PMS2 have a mildly reduced rate of mutations at A and T residues (Ijspeert et al. 2019). The reduction was less than that observed in patients lacking MSH2 or MSH6, indicating that an additional nicking enzyme may be coupled to MSH2:MSH6 in somatic hypermutation.
EXO1 interacts with MSH2 and MLH1 and therefore is presumed to interact with their respective heterodimers MSH2:MSH6 and MLH1:PMS2, forming a ternary complex with MLH1:PMS2 (Nielsen et al. 2004). EXO1 exonucleolytically degrades one strand in a 5' to 3' direction (Genschel et al. 2002, Genschel and Modrich 2003, Dzantiev et al. 2004, Zhang et al. 2005, Constantin et al. 2005, Genschel and Modrich 2006, Orans et al. 2011), creating a single -stranded gap extending 90-170 nucleotides beyond the mismatch (Fang and Modrich 1993). Error-prone DNA polymerases, notably POLH (DNA polymerase eta, Zeng et al. 2001, Zhao et al. 2013), associated with ubiquitinated PCNA (Ub-K164-PCNA) (Kannouche et al. 2004, Bienko et al. 2005) synthesize a strand of DNA across the gap created by EXO1. The recruitment and ubiquitination of PCNA are not well characterized.
After DNA is synthesized across the gap, a nick remains that is ligated by an unknown ligase that may be LIG1 or LIG3.
The mutation patterns in cultured human B cells deficient in UNG or mismatch repair indicate that UNG may excise a uridine residue exposed in the single-stranded gap generated by mismatch repair, reflecting the possible existence of a unique hybrid pathway involving both base excision and mismatch repair (Frieder et al. 2009).
